subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: protecting privacy when using AI [Thinking]
passage: Sohan was about to paste his whole profile into an AI tool to get tips for his science-fair speech: full name, address, school, marks from the last exam. His cursor hovered. Gurpreet leaned in. “Wait, you're putting your address in there?” Sohan stopped. He didn't know where the information went, who could read it, or how long it stayed. He deleted the first lines. I'll say: a Class 10 student, speech on solar cookers. No name, no address, no marks, no friends' names. He also removed a line about Gurpreet's project. He typed the general version and still got useful tips. On a sticky note on his monitor he wrote: Ask about ideas, not about me.

qa.q: What did Sohan write on the sticky note?
qa.a: Sohan wrote: Ask about ideas, not about me.

qa.q: What made Sohan stop and delete the details?
qa.a: Sohan felt uneasy because he did not know where the information went, who could read it or how long it stayed.

qa.q: What else could Sohan do to stay safe with such tools?
qa.a: Sohan could ask a parent or teacher about privacy settings before using a tool for anything personal.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet's privacy have been affected if the project line stayed in?
qa.a: Gurpreet's project details would have been shared without permission, so removing the line protects Gurpreet.

grounding: A student decides not to enter his full name, address, marks or friends' details into an AI tool, since he does not know how the information is stored or used.
